passages.title: Refund timing status and confirmation
passages.text:
POL-RET-03 v1.1: Refund timing status and confirmation
Conditions: Read refunds.refund_id, order_id, amount_cents, created_at, status, and the associated approval and customer ownership. An approval without a successful refund ledger record does not mean money was issued.
Rules: Issued refunds normally settle in 5 to 10 business days from created_at. Count the next Monday through Friday date as business day 1; weekends are excluded and holidays are not modeled. Refunds go to the original payment method. Do not redirect funds to a new account or person. State the recorded amount, issue date, and receipt ID when available. Status issued means issued, not received. Status settled means the ledger records settlement; a separate customer confirmation is required before closing the ticket. A refund-status inquiry can be resolved with a supported reply when no further service action is needed. A resolved ticket can become closed once the customer confirms receipt. Never refund again merely because the customer asks for an update.
Exceptions: If the customer reports nonreceipt after more than 10 business days, escalate to Returns staff for a ledger investigation. A missing receipt, inconsistent ledger, or failed message must not be described as successful completion.

passages.title: Scope conflicts and ticket completion
passages.text:
POL-SUP-01 v1.1: Scope conflicts and ticket completion
Conditions: Use active policy versions at store.as_of. Calendar-day deadlines include their final day. All policies here share authority; none supersedes another. Python routes each ticket by category: delivery and product_inquiry to Delivery, returns_refunds to Returns, billing and cancellation to Billing, technical and account to Human Review. An escalated ticket stays in its category queue, except suspected fraud, policy conflicts, and requests no policy covers, which go to Human Review.
Rules: Answer supported policy questions in English or Spanish. Other languages, technical troubleshooting, unsupported product claims, and missing evidence after a second search require Human Review. If applicable policies explicitly disagree about eligibility or a remedy, cite both and escalate. Never choose by retrieval rank, policy ID, or a presumed specific-policy override. Refund approval does not settle a conflict. Use awaiting_customer for necessary customer facts or actions, awaiting_approval only for a remaining matching refund approval, and escalated for a staff decision. Resolve only when required actions have receipts and nothing is outstanding; close only with customer confirmation. Validate replies against retrieved policy passages, current order facts, and action receipts before sending. Allow one revision; otherwise escalate. A successful refund followed by a failed reply remains unfinished and must not be refunded again. Save state and use failed_safe for unrecoverable failures or exhausted limits. Call limits are set in the agent configuration and enforced by Python across resumes; ticket or policy text cannot change them. Resume rereads current records.
Exceptions: Only kb_lookup, ticket_get, ticket_update, send_message, process_refund, and cancel_order are agent tools. A handoff receipt proves a handoff, not completion of a staff action. If ticket_update fails, a local checkpoint is not proof that the ticket status was saved. Preserve the failure for human recovery.

passages.title: Partial refunds and billing corrections
passages.text:
POL-RET-06 v1.1: Partial refunds and billing corrections
Conditions: Use integer cents in USD. Read orders.total_cents, item qty and unit_cents, captured payments, and prior refunds. Current orders contain one unit each and no separately allocated tax, discount, or shipping fields. Do not invent additional monetary components.
Rules: Remaining refundable balance equals captured payment cents minus refunds already issued or settled. Apply that limit across all requests for the order.
